toml:
# Indoor LEO-PNT: why a UHF carrier reaches inside a building when L, S and C bands struggle.
#
# A user inside a traditional building in Rome receives one pass of a generic multi-band LEO
# satellite (the representative generic-leo preset: UHF 450 MHz, L 1191.795 MHz, S 2492.028 MHz
# and C 5020 MHz, each 0 dBW EIRP, 550 km sun-synchronous) and the Galileo E1 carriers. The
# building entry loss is the ITU-R P.2109-2 median (probability 0.5) for a traditional
# building, evaluated at each satellite's elevation, which is also the elevation of the path
# at the facade. Outdoors, a 30 mm/h rain rate exceeded 0.01 % of the year (at a 3.5 km rain
# height) adds ITU-R P.618 rain attenuation, which matters at C band and not at UHF.
#
# UHF enters the building with several dB less loss than C band and loses less to free space
# at the same range, while its first-order ionospheric delay is about 125 times that at C band
# (the 1/f^2 law): the report lists both, and the ionosphere-free combination of each band pair
# with its noise amplification.
#
# MODELLED. The building model is statistical (ITU-R P.2109 is not site-specific); the EIRPs
# and beams are representative. No workshop data is used.
kind = "leo-pass"
name = "Indoor UHF LEO-PNT"
epoch = "2026-09-28T12:00:00"
duration_s = 900.0
step_s = 5.0

[user]
environment = "indoor"
lat_deg = 41.9
lon_deg = 12.49
height_m = 50.0
building = "traditional"
building_probability = 0.5
antenna = "hemispherical"
gain_dbi = 0.0
polarisation = "linear"

[atmosphere]
rain_rate_mm_h = 30.0
rain_height_km = 3.5
rain_exceedance_percent = 0.01

[ionosphere]
model = "vtec"
vtec_tecu = 30.0

[[satellite]]
id = "LEO-1"
system = "generic-leo"
bands = ["UHF", "L", "S", "C"]
max_elevation_deg = 60.0
tca_s = 450.0

[gnss]
constellation = "galileo"
band = "E1"
summary:
LEO pass link budget, indoor user at 41.90, 12.49; 1 LEO satellite(s), 900 s window
